div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 45px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 20px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 205px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 146px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Under God's justice, which is greater/heavier: sin or righteousness/repentance?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 148px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: God is perfectly just: the wages of sin is death, and there is no forgiveness of sins without shedding blood (ie. some punishment or sacrifice). Since sanctifying grace is a participation in God's own life, it can't be recreated or restored by our finite efforts in righteousness and repentance; only a perfect being can restore it (ie. through Christ's perfect righteousness and vicarious atonement, whose resurrection defeated the penalty of death on our behalf).

This is why no amount of righteousness or repentance can undo, revert, or otherwise pardon the guilt and penalty of even a single sin. This is also why Adam's sin (and ours) wasn't temporally forgiven - for its natural consequence is ongoing earthly toil, suffering, and separation from perfect communion with God - and how we're all able to be saved due to Christ's redeeming grace.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 148px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: God is the Just: every action, no matter how big or small, will be taken into account, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. God is also the Oft-Forgiving, Most-Loving:
we're held accountable only to our knowledge and intentions, and

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: the path to forgiveness is opened before the path to punishment. As a result, God multiplies good deeds out of His mercy (while bad deeds are recorded as they are), erases previous sins with sincere repentance (even turning them into good deeds), and valuing lasting deeds of righteousness to outweigh isolated slips.

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: This is why Adam's sin was only a slip in God's eyes - a momentary lapse of judgement between consistent obedience and sincere repentance (all willfully done) - and why he was forgiven once he turned back to God (which is the same for us as well).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 204px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 148px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Sin > righteousness/repentance

div.span: vs.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 370px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 176px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: How is God's mercy revealed within His justice?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 285px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 178px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Sin must be punished, but God willingly took its burden for our sake

div.span: God expects perfect obedience to His will, and because God's justice is perfect, the debt of every sin must be satisfied. But since every sin is also against an infinite God,
the penalty of sin is death (separation from God) -

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: its weight far beyond our finite capacity to repay (or to recreate that grace) by our own righteousness or repentance.

Yet, out of His love and desire for our salvation, God reveals His mercy by sending Christ - who lived sinlessly, willingly bore the penalty for our sins on our behalf (ie. death), and defeated it through his resurrection

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: (despite us being undeserving of it)

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: . In this way, both perfect justice and mercy are expressed: sin is truly punished, but its punishment is willingly borne by Christ instead of falling on us - allowing forgiveness to occur without compromising justice. As a result, our righteousness and repentance do not pay for sin, but follow as participation in Christ's

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: perfection - with the eligibility for that mercy starting with our faith and trust in what he has done for us.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 251px; height: 1px; padding-top: 285px; margin-left: 437px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 178px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: Righteousness is rewarded while sin is punished, with God forgiving instead of punishing

div.span: God expects a minimal standard of worship and obedience, expressed by faith, repentance, and righteousness - within one's real capacity (which is known and determined by God for each person). As such, every person is held fully accountable only to their own deeds, with all actions personally owned and proportionally weighed under God's Justice: righteousness is rewarded and sin is punished.
Yet, out of His love and mercy, God opens the path to forgiveness before punishment by delaying penalty - multiplying good deeds, recording sins only as they are,

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: rewarding excellence in superfluous good deeds,

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: and erasing (even transforming) sins through sincere repentance and restitution to the best of one’s ability.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: In this way, both perfect justice and mercy are expressed: each person receives exactly what they are accountable for, while God not dismissing or wasting the sincere righteous actions of believers - with the promise of sincere repentance being a direct doorway to forgiveness.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 369px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 178px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Sins are punished; forgiveness occurs after/by means of Christ willingly bearing the punishment on our behalf

div.span: vs.

span.b: Righteousness is rewarded while sins are punished; forgiveness occurs before/instead of punishment

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 158px; height: 1px; padding-top: 563px; margin-left: 21px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 191px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;

font.b: What do the differences reveal about God and His justice and mercy?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 482px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 33px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 482px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 33px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Justice requires sin to be satisfied by punishment or sacrifice before forgiveness can occur.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 482px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 33px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Justice requires surplus righteousness or sincere repentance
before
forgiveness can occur.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 482px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 33px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Punishment always occurs

div.span: vs.

span.b: Forgiveness waives punishment

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 519px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 38px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: As a result of God's justice:

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 519px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 38px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Sin incurs a debt greater than the merit of any righteousness and repentance a person can do (for any sin is against the infinite God).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 519px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 38px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Sincere righteousness and repentance is rewarded and multiplied (by God's mercy) - unlike sins, which are recorded as is.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 519px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 38px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Mercy is not embedded in the law

div.span: vs.

span.b: Mercy is embedded in the law

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 562px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 43px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: As a result of God's mercy:

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 562px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 43px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Jesus Christ - God in the human Person - willingly bore sin's debt for us (out of his love).

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 562px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 43px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: God delays punishment to give us abundant opportunities to be forgiven first - with
sincere repentance able to erase and transform sins

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 562px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 43px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: God bore sin's penalty for us

div.span: vs.

span.b: We bear both our righteousness (including repentance) and sins

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 622px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: As a result of what God holds us accountable to:

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 622px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: We can't satisfy the debt of sin ourselves, so our salvation ultimately depends on God's grace in Christ's atonement and our faith in him to be justified/eligible for that grace.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Even with faith in Christ, righteousness (with confession) is still required to keep & participate in God's grace - but it is not why we are saved.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 622px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Our actions are personally and proportionally weighed, where our salvation depends on our faith, righteousness, and repentance - within the capacity God decreed for each of us.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: With faith in God, He accepts our sincere repentance, erases our sins, and multiplies our good deeds - thus waiving the punishment.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 622px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Salvation is grounded in Christ's righteousness, not our own

div.span: vs.

span.b: Salvation is grounded in God's mercy by weighing our own faith, righteousness, and repentance against our sins

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Our actions are a sign of our moral values.

div.span: This ties moral evaluation to what we do, not what we claim (or feel) - the basis for accountability and justice.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Actions are a participation in God's grace and perfection.

div.span: Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead - even demons believe in God. As such, righteousness is the necessary fruit and evidence of faith: if it is missing, then it reveals a necessary deficiency in faith. This makes it a strong fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Actions are the external expression of one's internal submission to God.

div.span: The requirement for God's forgiveness is faith and righteousness, such that
the first people condemned by God are the hypocrites who claim to believe in Him but don't do so in their actions. This makes it a strong fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 702px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Righteousness is a sign of inner faith (strong fit)
vs.
Righteousness is a sign of inner faith (strong fit)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 777px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: "We have a disposition towards concepts of justice."

div.span: This expects people to be held accountable to their choices, where the guilty bear a proportional cost - and the innocent are not punished.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 777px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Justice is debt-centric: sin creates a spiritual debt that must be satisfied - such that it can be paid for by an eligible substitute.

div.span: Sin causes debt, but an eligible innocent can pay it instead of the guilty.
This means that the essence of justice is settlement (with gratitude & love), not accountability - a weak fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 777px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Justice is credit-centric: both the debt of sin and reward of righteousness are borne only by the guilty.

div.span: Every soul bears its own burden - accountable only to their choices: those guilty of sin will receive its due, and those guilty of righteousness will receive its due - a strong fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 777px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
Justice is about debt/settlement
(weak fit)
vs.

Justice is about credit/accountability
(strong fit)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 852px; margin-left: 182px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

b.font: "Falsehood is easier and more common, while good is harder and more valued."

div.span: This comes from the observation that righteousness (like order) requires personal maintenance - while sin (like disorder) requires personal neglect.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 852px; margin-left: 322px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Human righteousness is harder, but it cannot outweigh human sin.

div.span: Sin causes our ineligibility for salvation, while good can't restore it - but Christ's perfection can.
This means that the essence of good's value is restricted to God's goodness, not the effort it requires - making it a partial fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 181px; height: 1px; padding-top: 852px; margin-left: 507px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.b: Human righteousness is harder, therefore it outweighs human sin.

div.span: Evil is easier and more common, but good is weighted more strongly in judgement - precisely because God embeds His mercy in the judgement and values more the hard path and sincere return. This makes it a strong fit with this inference.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 136px; height: 1px; padding-top: 852px; margin-left: 692px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 73px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;

font.b: Islam accomplishes everything the Christian Jesus does, but with a more original and perfect form of accountability, consistency, and better fitting the mold of a "loving father" - allowing a stronger case for coherence to be built.

div.font: At its root, the fundamental difference between the two narratives is how God’s justice is oriented (debt vs. credit) - and the basis for salvation (including how God responds to Adam's sin) follows from that.

For Christianity’s justice, all sins must be paid for. The core "debt of [human] sin" (loss of sanctifying grace) sits in a higher tier than any act of human righteousness: no amount of good deeds can recreate that grace - only participating in it (only if restored by God) - which is what God shows by expelling Adam from Eden. But, out of His mercy, God Himself satisfies this debt on our behalf through Christ - certainly revealing God's love for us. However, it also exposes concepts such as an innocent bearing the burden of the guilty (both in Adam’s descendants sharing the debt of his act and in Christ satisfying the debt for us), sin’s debt being valued in a higher category than righteousness’ credit (despite God's mercy), and God’s treatment of Adam after his sin being different than Christ's (ie. God in the human Person) treatment of sincere believers after their sins - each challenging our predisposition towards accountability and justice.

Meanwhile, Islam’s justice holds each person fully accountable for their own actions - crediting both sins and good deeds - with God, out of His mercy, valuing our sincere righteousness and repentance over our sins. God's relationship with Adam is the same as His relationship with us today: Adam sins, repents, and is forgiven, and is placed on earth fully forgiven and pure while being judged only for his own choices. As a result, this narrative does not accept concepts such as an innocent bearing the burden of the guilty (which would be unjust) or sin being valued more than righteousness (which would contradict God’s mercy and align with Satan’s desire for us to despair of it).

div.span: Therefore: even though both affirm God's justice and mercy/love, Islam's narrative cleanly fits our natural disposition for personal accountability while Christianity's narrative leads to concepts that don't cleanly fit. Moreover, the Islamic God is more consistent and better fits the mold of a "loving father", treating Adam the same way He treats us: with original forgiveness, mercy, and justice. As a result, Islam better fits reality.
